And a day of, yeah, just a day of general sort of hijinks and stuff.
sentences.zh: 也是一个，嗯，总之就是各种胡闹和玩乐的日子。

sentences.en: So I thought Gilbert and Sullivan would be a great place to come in.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为吉尔伯特与萨利文会是一个很好的切入点。

sentences.en: So Gilbert and Sullivan, the great kind of Victorian sort of light opera stars of British popular culture, incredibly popular around the world, particularly in America.
sentences.zh: 吉尔伯特与萨利文，英国流行文化中维多利亚时代的轻歌剧巨星，在世界各地都极其受欢迎，尤其是在美国。

sentences.en: So if you look at the list of kind of amateur performances and things of Gilbert and Sullivan plays, I mean, the number in America is mind-boggling.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看美国业余演出吉尔伯特与萨利文剧目的名单，我是说，那个数量简直令人难以置信。

sentences.en: But their very first play, Tom, it's a Greek theme, you see.
sentences.zh: 但他们的第一部剧，汤姆，它是希腊主题的，你看。

sentences.en: That's why I thought, that's why I picked it.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我选了它。

sentences.en: So their very first collaboration in 1871, starting on Boxing Day 1871.
sentences.zh: 他们第一次合作是在1871年，从1871年的节礼日开始。

sentences.en: That's the day it opened, is it?
Yes, the day it opened.
The Gaiety Theatre was an opera called Thespis, or The Gods Grown Old.
sentences.zh: 在盖蒂剧院上演的歌剧叫《塞斯庇斯》，或者叫《诸神老去》。

sentences.en: So you've got these two characters.
You've got Gilbert, who's a bit older, who's the son of a naval surgeon.
sentences.zh: 一个是吉尔伯特，年纪稍大，是一位海军外科医生的儿子。

sentences.en: He does the words.
And Sullivan, who's a great composer, son of a military bandmaster, who was born in 1842, and he does the music.
sentences.zh: 还有萨利文，一位伟大的作曲家，一位军乐队指挥的儿子，出生于1842年，他负责作曲。

sentences.en: Now, Sullivan sees himself as a sort of serious composer, which he was.
sentences.zh: 萨利文把自己看作是一位严肃的作曲家，他也确实是。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, he's always, you know, he's sort of...
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，他总是，你知道，他有点……

sentences.en: It's the classic thing.
He's out with a comedian.
sentences.zh: 他和一个喜剧演员混在一起。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's the classic thing.
It's sort of Strathcone and Doyle trying to escape Sherlock Holmes.
sentences.zh: 就像斯特拉康和道尔试图摆脱夏洛克·福尔摩斯一样。

sentences.en: Sullivan is always slightly trying to escape Gilbert and Sullivan.
sentences.zh: 萨利文总是稍微有点想摆脱吉尔伯特与萨利文的束缚。

sentences.en: But Gilbert kind of drags him back in with his stories of magic lozenges and things of this pirate.
sentences.zh: 但吉尔伯特总是用他那些关于魔法润喉糖和海盗的故事把他拉回来。

sentences.en: And schoolgirls and...
Yeah, all of this sort of stuff.
So they get brought together to work on this opera.
sentences.zh: 所以他们被凑在一起创作这部歌剧。

sentences.en: It's basically a Christmas entertainment.
sentences.zh: 它基本上就是一场圣诞娱乐节目。

sentences.en: The plan is for it to just run for a few weeks or months.
sentences.zh: 计划只是演几周或几个月。

sentences.en: It is advertised as an entirely original grotesque opera in two acts.
sentences.zh: 它被宣传为一部两幕的“完全原创的怪诞歌剧”。

sentences.en: I like that, the grotesque opera.
A grotesque opera.
If you were going into an opera, you want it to be pretty grotesque, I think.
sentences.zh: 如果你要去看歌剧，我想你会希望它足够怪诞。

sentences.en: Yeah.
So the story, do you want to know the story, Tom?
sentences.zh: 那么故事，汤姆，你想知道故事内容吗？

sentences.en: Well, so Thespis is the first actor.
sentences.zh: 嗯，塞斯庇斯是第一位演员。

sentences.en: Yeah, the father of drama.
Is he the first actor or...
He's the person who first acts in a tragedy.
sentences.zh: 他是第一个在悲剧中表演的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
So the plan is...
So the story is that basically the gods have grown elderly on Mount Olympus.
sentences.zh: 故事基本上是说奥林匹斯山上的诸神已经老了。

sentences.en: And they're just bored and they feel like no one listens to them anymore.
sentences.zh: 他们感到无聊，觉得没人再听他们的了。

sentences.en: And is this set in ancient Greece or in...
sentences.zh: 这是设定在古希腊还是……

sentences.en: Yeah, in ancient Greece.
It's not modern Greece.
Okay.
So they fancy a change and they decide that they will swap places with Thespis and his actors.
sentences.zh: 他们想换换口味，决定和塞斯庇斯以及他的演员们互换身份。

sentences.en: So the actors will come up to Olympus and the story is basically them trying to rule the universe.
sentences.zh: 所以演员们会去奥林匹斯山，故事基本上就是他们试图统治宇宙。

sentences.en: And they are terrible at it.
And does hilarity into you?
It does.
So the replacement...
Do you know the replacement for Mars?
sentences.zh: 你知道战神马尔斯的替代者是谁吗？

sentences.en: Do you know what his name is?
sentences.zh: 你知道他叫什么名字吗？

sentences.en: Timidon.
Oh, that's...
And Timidon.
Do you know what's so comic about this?
sentences.zh: 你知道这有什么好笑的吗？

sentences.en: He's a pacifiSt.
He's a pacifiSt.
It's hilarious.
Yeah.
The substitute for Hymen.
The kind of goddess of...
What is she?
The goddess of marriage.
Yeah.
She doesn't want to marry anybody.
That's the joke.
She's a confirmed spinster.
And the guy who's replacing Pluto.
sentences.zh: 还有那个接替冥王普鲁托的人。

sentences.en: Is this Spenthrift?
No, he doesn't like anybody dying.
sentences.zh: 不，他不希望任何人死去。

sentences.en: Doesn't want to let anybody die.
Doesn't want anyone to come to the underworld.
sentences.zh: 不想让任何人来到冥界。

sentences.en: God, hilarity doesn't ensue.
Yeah, it's mayhem.
It's absolute mayhem.
It's hilarious.
The gods down on Earth...
It's just what you want to have a boxing day.
sentences.zh: 这正是你圣诞节后第一天想看的。

sentences.en: The gods down on Earth are shocked by this, carry on.
sentences.zh: 下凡到人间的众神对此感到震惊，继续说吧。

sentences.en: And they return to Olympus and they kick out the actors and they say, go back to Earth.
sentences.zh: 他们回到奥林匹斯山，把演员们赶走，说：回地球去吧。

sentences.en: Your fate is to become eminent tragedians who no one ever goes to see.
sentences.zh: 你们的命运就是成为没人去看的杰出悲剧演员。

sentences.en: That's funny.
That's still funny.
And that's what happens.
So it runs...
So this opens on Boxing Day and it runs for 63 performances.
sentences.zh: 这部剧在节礼日首演，一共演了63场。

sentences.en: Which is a success.
Which is a great success.
And everybody thinks...
A lot of people think it's very funny.
sentences.zh: 很多人觉得它非常有趣。

sentences.en: Well, the public think it's funny, but the critics are not terribly impressed.
sentences.zh: 嗯，观众觉得有趣，但评论家们并不怎么买账。

sentences.en: So do you want to hear a couple of the reviews?
Yeah.
A publication called The Hornet.
sentences.zh: 有一份叫《大黄蜂》（The Hornet）的刊物。

sentences.en: You wouldn't want to be reviewed by The Hornet.
sentences.zh: 你可不想被《大黄蜂》评论。

sentences.en: You wouldn't.
So the problem is they review only the premiere and the premiere is much, much too long.
sentences.zh: 问题是他们只评论了首演，而首演实在太长、太长了。

sentences.en: So in the sort of the adverts, the management of the Gaiety Theatre have said, you must book your carriages for 11 o'clock.
sentences.zh: 所以在广告里，盖伊蒂剧院的管理层说：请务必在11点预订马车。

sentences.en: But it's gone past 12 and the play is still going on at midnight.
sentences.zh: 但已经过了12点，戏还在演，午夜时分还在演。

sentences.en: But the japery is still going on at midnight.
sentences.zh: 午夜时分，闹剧还在继续。

sentences.en: So the Hornet...
The Hornets...
The play is actually called Thespis or The Gods Grown Old.
sentences.zh: 这部戏其实叫《泰斯庇斯，或众神老矣》。

sentences.en: But the headline on the Hornets review is Thespis, The Gods Grown Old and Wearisome in capital letters.
sentences.zh: 但《大黄蜂》评论的标题是大写的《泰斯庇斯，众神老矣且令人厌倦》。

sentences.en: And the morning advertiser says, It is a dreary, tedious, two-act rigmarole of a plot.
sentences.zh: 而《晨报》说：这是一部沉闷、冗长、两幕剧的胡言乱语。

sentences.en: Grotesque without wit and the music thin without liveliness.
sentences.zh: 怪诞而无趣，音乐单薄且毫无生气。

sentences.en: The curtain falls before a yawning and weary audience.
sentences.zh: 幕布落下时，面对的是一群哈欠连天、疲惫不堪的观众。

sentences.en: But apart from that, how did you enjoy the play?
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，你觉得这戏怎么样？

sentences.en: So the music, I think, is loSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，音乐可能失传了。

sentences.en: That's why I can't sing it, much as I would like to.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我没法唱，尽管我很想唱。

sentences.en: Oh, that is a shame.
Because obviously at that point, no one knows that Gilbert and Sullivan is going to turn out into this tremendous franchise.
sentences.zh: 因为显然在当时，没人知道吉尔伯特与萨利文后来会成为如此巨大的品牌。

sentences.en: But how come they haven't kept the music?
sentences.zh: 但他们怎么没把音乐留下来呢？

sentences.en: How come they haven't kept the music?
sentences.zh: 他们怎么没把音乐留下来呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
I don't know.
I think Sullivan just probably dashed it off.
sentences.zh: 我想萨利文可能只是随手写写。

sentences.en: Knocked it off.
Yeah, just thought this is a load of old tosh.
sentences.zh: 是啊，就觉得这堆东西全是垃圾。

sentences.en: Make some money out of it.
Quite odd not to have kept it, though.
sentences.zh: 没留下来确实挺奇怪的。

sentences.en: Well, I don't know.
I mean, I don't claim to be a Sullivan-ologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我不敢自称是萨利文研究专家。

sentences.en: So anyway, the next thing is a thing called Trial by Jury.
sentences.zh: 总之，下一部作品叫《陪审团审判》。

sentences.en: That's, I think, reasonably successful.
And then they get into the world of topsy-turvy-dom.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就进入了“颠倒世界”的领域。

sentences.en: Do you know, have you seen the film Topsy-turvy?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，你看过电影《颠倒乾坤》吗？

sentences.en: No.
It's great, actually.
Is that the V?
Mike Lee film?
No, I haven't.
It's really good.
I've never seen the Gilbert and Sullivan.
sentences.zh: 我从没看过吉尔伯特与萨利文的作品。

sentences.en: I don't know anything about them.
I mean, I do, because I vaguely know.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我知道一点，因为我隐约听说过。

sentences.en: Paris of Penzance.
Very model of a modern major general.
The Mikado.
A short, sharp shock.
Yeah.
It's the kind of thing, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想大概就是这类东西吧。

sentences.en: I think Gilbert and Sullivan, for people of our generation, is slightly tainted, because it's the kind of thing that's very unlovely.
sentences.zh: 我觉得对于我们这一代人来说，吉尔伯特与萨利文有点被玷污了，因为这东西听起来很不讨喜。

sentences.en: Pomp-dee-dee-pomp-dee-dee-pomp-dee-pomp.
I think Gilbert and Sullivan would recite at Tory party conferences as part of an attack on single mothers.
sentences.zh: 我觉得吉尔伯特与萨利文会被保守党大会拿来朗诵，作为攻击单身母亲的一部分。

sentences.en: Yes.
It was Peter Lilly, wasn't it?
It was.
He sung a bit at Gilbert and Sullivan, and the audience loved it, but the rest of the country was absolutely important.
sentences.zh: 他唱了一段吉尔伯特与萨利文，观众很喜欢，但全国其他地方的人都惊呆了。

sentences.en: Vomited and voted for Tony Blair.
sentences.zh: 呕吐之后投给了托尼·布莱尔。

sentences.en: Yes.
But I think Gilbert and Sullivan is very jolly.
sentences.zh: 但我认为吉尔伯特与萨利文非常欢快。

sentences.en: It's all sort of gentle satire of institutions and so on, which still stands up to me.
sentences.zh: 这都是些对体制之类的温和讽刺，我觉得现在依然站得住脚。

sentences.en: So should I watch one?
Would you recommend I should?
I think the Mikado is, I think you should watch Topsy Turvy, the film, because that is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 我觉得《天皇》……我认为你应该看《颠倒乾坤》那部电影，因为那部太精彩了。

sentences.en: Okay.
Jim Broadbent is...
Do I need to know about it?
sentences.zh: 我需要了解相关背景吗？

sentences.en: No, you can know nothing about it at all.
sentences.zh: 不用，你完全不需要了解任何背景。

sentences.en: Okay, I'll do that.
It's a brilliant recreation of Victorian England and of that world.
sentences.zh: 那是对维多利亚时代英国及其世界的精彩重现。

sentences.en: And then the most famous ones are probably the Pirates of Penzance and the Mikado.
sentences.zh: 然后最出名的可能就是《彭赞斯的强盗》和《天皇》了。

sentences.en: And the Mikado, yeah.
The Mikado is now in danger, isn't it?
It's been seen as the ultimate cultural appropriation, because it's all about Japan.
sentences.zh: 它被视为终极文化挪用，因为它讲的全是日本的事。

sentences.en: Three little maids.
Three little maids are we?
Three little maids.
I don't know the words, but that's how it goes.
sentences.zh: 我不记得歌词了，但大概是这样。

sentences.en: Anyway, I've seen the Mikado and it's very jolly.
sentences.zh: 总之，我看过《天皇》，非常欢快。

sentences.en: They're Chinese, aren't they?
No, Japanese, of course.
They're Japanese.
So Gilbert had been to an exhibition of Japanese sort of arts and stuff, and that gave him the idea for the Mikado.
sentences.zh: 所以吉尔伯特当时去看了日本艺术之类的展览，这给了他创作《天皇》的灵感。

sentences.en: But it's actually not about Japan.
sentences.zh: 但它其实并不是关于日本的。

sentences.en: I mean, the joke is, it's a kind of parody of...
sentences.zh: 我是说，笑点在于，这是一种对……的戏仿。

sentences.zh: 那个伟大的普巴（Pooh-Bah）就像公务员一样。

sentences.en: I mean, it's clearly, it's a bit like The Importance of Being Earnest, or that you don't have to have seen it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这很明显，有点像《认真的重要性》，你不需要非得看过它。

sentences.en: It kind of floats around as, you know, vaguely synthesized ideas.
sentences.zh: 它就像某种模糊的合成概念一样流传着。

sentences.en: And there are these idioms, like a short, sharp shock, that have sort of penetrated into the language because of Gilbert and Sullivan, and are actually just as popular in America.
sentences.zh: 还有一些习语，比如“短促而尖锐的打击”，因为吉尔伯特与萨利文而进入了语言中，而且在美国也同样流行。

sentences.en: So you'll see loads of references to it in kind of, you know, that sort of kind of American, tweet the American columnist who will quote Gilbert and Sullivan.
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到很多引用，比如那种美国专栏作家会引用吉尔伯特与萨利文。

sentences.en: Yes.
So the Mikado is genuinely problematic, is it?
sentences.zh: 所以《天皇》真的有问题吗？

sentences.en: I don't think it is genuinely problematic because people fought back against its cancellation because they pointed out it's not meant to be about Japan.
sentences.zh: 我不认为它真的有问题，因为人们反抗了它的取消，因为他们指出它本意并非关于日本。

It's about Britain.

sentences.en: Well, that's very, that's very up to date, satire.
